revision: Three-card native horizontal viewport over four actual supplied cards with actual creature GLB
assessmentType: Independent subjective visual assessment of the current three-visible-card carousel, its first and last windows, actual supplied artwork, discovery controls and actual creature balance. Native interaction behavior is supported by separate test artifacts. This score is not an objective pixel-match score or a GPU/frame-pacing benchmark.

rubric.category: Actual supplied artwork and focal cropping
rubric.notes: All four actual supplied card images remain. Both visible windows preserve each image's established portrait crop and source identity, without stretching. No image regeneration or retouching is introduced.

rubric.category: Three-card viewport geometry and endpoint composition
rubric.notes: A 751px viewport fits exactly three 247x373 cards with 5px gaps at 1280x720. Initial New/Resume/Load Game and terminal Resume/Load Game/Browse windows are complete, with no neighbor bleed or clones. Endpoints clamp without wrapping.

rubric.category: Text, selected borders and discovery controls
rubric.notes: Text and selected outlines remain visible in both windows. The final dark control backplate resolves the counter's earlier low contrast over the patterned gold robe. Enabled arrows are brighter than disabled endpoints. Controls remain separated from the controller footer.

rubric.category: Actual creature balance behind the carousel
rubric.notes: The narrower visible row exposes more of the actual model's shoulder and torso while preserving the behind-card relationship. Crown, eye, orbital rings, raised arm and robe form a clear silhouette. Intentional outer arm and robe cropping remains.
The cold source images, teal particle halos and actual creature remain coherent against warm gold fog. More visible torso improves the scene's balance. Particle placement varies with animation.

Separate carousel verification covers wheel, real Chromium touch, keyboard, gamepad, endpoint clamping, resize and reduced motion. Native scroll traces contain intermediate positions. The corrected clip demonstrates actual-model first-to-last-to-first windows. Shared software-GPU load makes traces sparse and the recorded frame pacing unsuitable for a smoothness or hardware-performance benchmark.

iterationHistory.findings: Card geometry, source crops, selected outlines and creature balance were good. Critic requested stronger discovery-control contrast over the patterned robe.

Initial clip spent most time loading and did not demonstrate both carousel windows. Critic requested a recording after the actual GLB was ready, with first-to-last-to-first windows and loading lead-in removed.

Final dark discovery-control backplate is readable at both desktop resolutions. Corrected video samples show actual-model initial, terminal and return windows without the loading prefix. No further visual changes required.

The demonstration clip uses reduced resolution and Low particle quality to show both actual-model windows under the capture environment's limits.

verdict: Meets the subjective 9/10 visual target for the three-visible-card native carousel over four actual supplied cards, with actual creature GLB. Native input behavior is verified separately; target-device frame pacing remains unbenchmarked.
